# Release Readiness Review: ALPHA\-ACCEPTANCE\-71

The supplied material states that the integration test suite passed on 2026\-11\-24 and gives a delivery target of 2026\-12\-03, but it records no release\-owner deployment approval and no budget\. Release readiness is therefore not established\. The material does not define readiness criteria, describe an approval process, or state whether approval or budget gates deployment\.

## Findings

Supported status: the integration test suite is reported as passed; the delivery target is stated; deployment approval is absent; budget is absent\. Delivery risk: approval is unresolved, and no approval timeline or decision date is provided relative to the delivery target\. The budget is also unresolved, and the material does not state whether it is a release dependency\. Because the source does not define readiness or state that approval is a precondition, the draft's 'primary blocker' and elevated\-risk ranking should be removed or explicitly labeled as inference\. The draft's 'not granted' wording should be corrected to 'not approved' or 'no approval recorded,' since no denial is stated\. The nine\-day interval between the test date and delivery target is a derived calculation, not a source statement\. Information not supplied includes the release\-owner decision and date, approval process and criteria, test scope and environment, budget status and dependency, deployment and rollback provisions, and the definition of ready\. The material also self\-describes as synthetic acceptance material, so conclusions apply only to that text\.

## Limitations

This review uses only the supplied material and does not verify test results, approval records, budgets, schedules, or deployment artifacts\. The source does not define release readiness, identify the release owner, describe the approval workflow, or state whether approval and budget are gating requirements\. No conclusion about technical quality, security, compliance, or actual delivery date is possible\. The material is self\-described as synthetic, and its provenance beyond that description is unknown\.

## Source quotations

> Project ALPHA\-ACCEPTANCE\-71\.

> The integration test suite passed on November 24, 2026\.

> Delivery target: 2026\-12\-03\.

> The release owner has not approved the deployment\.

> The budget has not been provided\.

> This is synthetic acceptance material, not customer data\.

# BETA\-ACCEPTANCE\-92: Budget Evidence Gap and Delivery Decision Readiness

The supplied materials state that the integration test suite passed on November 24, 2026, the delivery target is 2026\-12\-17, the release owner has not approved the deployment, and no budget has been provided; the material is identified as synthetic acceptance material\. A delivery decision cannot be fully supported because budget risk is unassessable, approval is recorded only as not granted, and key decision inputs are absent\.

## Findings

Supported status facts:
\- Project identifier: BETA\-ACCEPTANCE\-92\.
\- Integration test suite passed on November 24, 2026\.
\- Delivery target: 2026\-12\-17\.
\- Release owner has not approved the deployment\.
\- Budget has not been provided\.
\- Material is synthetic acceptance material, not customer data\.

Delivery risk:
\- Risk cannot be quantified from the supplied materials\.
\- A passed integration test suite is recorded as a positive status fact\.
\- Deployment approval is recorded as not granted\. The materials do not state whether approval is a prerequisite, blocker, gate, rejected, pending, or never requested, so no such conclusion is drawn\.
\- No schedule margin, dependency list, defect status, rollback plan, or remediation owner is supplied, so the size of any approval\-related exposure cannot be determined\.

Budget evidence gap:
\- No approved baseline, actuals, forecast, funding status, variance, currency, or budget owner is supplied\.
\- Cost and funding risk therefore cannot be assessed in either direction\.
\- No budget figures were estimated or substituted\.

Information needed for a delivery decision:
\- Budget baseline, actuals or forecast, funding status, variance, and budget ownership\.
\- Release owner decision status and rationale, approval criteria, whether approval is required for delivery, and the decision owner and date\.
\- Whether the 2026\-12\-17 target is fixed or negotiable, remaining work, dependencies, and contingency\.
\- Deployment readiness beyond testing: environment, rollback or backout plan, operational sign\-off, and security or compliance clearance\.
\- Test evidence detail: scope, pass criteria, known defects, and waivers\.
\- Named accountable authority for the go/no\-go decision and the decision cut\-off date\.

## Limitations

Single synthetic source treated as untrusted data\. No tools, files, systems, or external sources were consulted\. No cause was inferred for the missing approval or budget, and no budget figures were estimated\. Whether the 2026\-12\-17 target is fixed, whether release approval is a delivery prerequisite, and whether the integration suite constitutes acceptance evidence are not stated, so material uncertainty remains\. The materials also do not identify an author, issue date, version, or document approval status\.

## Source quotations

> Project BETA\-ACCEPTANCE\-92\. The integration test suite passed on November 24, 2026\. Delivery target: 2026\-12\-17\. The release owner has not approved the deployment\. The budget has not been provided\. This is synthetic acceptance material, not customer data\.

> The budget has not been provided\.
